layers.title: Times foreign investors sued this country under investment treaties
layers.plain: How many treaty lawsuits foreign investors have brought against this country, added up over 1987 to 2025. This is a total across all those years, and it covers only cases that became public. The count is partial. A blank country does not mean zero: it means its page could not be read, or the page that opened did not show cases against it. A zero appears only for Mali and Togo, whose UNCTAD pages say "No cases available." Countries left blank for those reasons: Afghanistan, Andorra, Antigua and Barbuda, Austria, Bahamas, Bhutan, Botswana, Brazil, Brunei, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Dominica, Eritrea, Eswatini, Fiji, Grenada, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Haiti, Hong Kong, Iceland, Ireland, Israel, Jamaica, Japan, Kiribati, Kosovo, Liberia, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Malawi, Maldives, Marshall Islands, Mauritania, Micronesia, Monaco, Namibia, Nauru, New Zealand, Niger, North Korea, Palau, Palestine, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Samoa, San Marino, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Singapore, Solomon Islands, Somalia, South Sudan, Suriname, Taiwan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu, United Kingdom, Vanuatu, Zambia, and dependent territories. Japan, Luxembourg and the United Kingdom are blank even though UNCTAD lists at least one case against each, because their full lists were not shown.
layers.source: UNCTAD Investment Dispute Settlement Navigator (partial read)
layers.how: One row per case on each country page of the UNCTAD Navigator, counting only cases where the country is the respondent. Rows were read through a web-reading tool that returns a short answer, not the raw table, so they were not checked against a downloaded file. n is the row count that tool reported. The Mali page says the Navigator is updated to 31 December 2025, but copies of different pages differ in age: "read_from" and flag other_page_copy show which address was read, and year_last shows the newest case seen. Mexico was 52 rows at one address and 61 at another; the 61 is used. Panama's page lists Enel Fortuna v. Panama twice, so n is 23 distinct cases, flagged. Croatia came back as a prose summary, flagged. A case with several respondents counts once for each. Round 25 added the countries in new_in_this_round. Their page numbers were wrong in the earlier try: many were one too high, and the same page can open at one address form and refuse another, so a refusal does not show that a number is wrong. Zeros taken only from pages showing rows where the country is the investor's home were removed in the check, because Japan, Luxembourg and the United Kingdom each had such a page and UNCTAD lists a case against each. A zero remains only where the page says "No cases available" (Mali, Togo).
layers.publish_reason: Publish as partial, with zeros removed. Row counts matched on all 25 spot-checked countries (Cambodia was replaced by Bolivia in the sample because its page would not open; its one case was confirmed on its case page), and outcomes matched on all 21 where outcomes were compared, apart from one unreturned outcome (Dunkeld v. Belize (I)). Each of UNCTAD's 2023 top ten is equal or lower than the count here, as expected over two later years. Still partial: 127 countries plus the EU against 136 plus the EU.

layers.title: Money foreign investors demanded from this country
layers.plain: The dollars investors asked for in those treaty lawsuits, added up over 1987 to 2025. This is what they demanded, not what they received, and many cases publish no figure. A blank country does not mean zero: no figure was read for it, or none is published.
layers.source: UNCTAD Investment Dispute Settlement Navigator (partial read)
layers.how: Sum of the amount fields on the same rows, USD-labelled amounts only, in whole US dollars. Amounts in other currencies are kept in other_currency_m in millions and not converted, so n understates countries sued mainly in euros or local currency (Spain, Czechia, Poland). A case with no published amount adds nothing; cases_with_amount gives how many had one. Venezuela has n null because the tool returned numbers with no currency; they are in unlabelled_m. Italy and the EU are absent because the tool returned no amounts for them, which does not mean none are published. Mexico amounts use the USD figure UNCTAD prints beside local-currency amounts. Settled amounts are included where the page gives them in the awarded field. For round 25 countries the USD figure UNCTAD prints beside a local-currency amount is used, the same way as Mexico earlier, so the earlier understatement for euro and local-currency countries does not apply to them. Russia, Slovakia, Thailand, Nepal and Cambodia are absent because the address that opened showed no amount columns. Fin.Co.Ge.Ro v. Romania came back with 327.00 mln EUR (362.60 mln USD) in the awarded field beside a state win, which looks like a misread, so it is left out of both money layers.
layers.publish_reason: Do not publish. The figures that were read match the pages, but the sums are on mixed bases. Earlier rounds summed only USD-labelled amounts and dropped the USD figure UNCTAD prints beside other currencies; later rounds used it. In the spot-check Albania shows $90.4 million claimed against $1,260.7 million printed, Bulgaria $1,206 million against $2,253.4 million, while Cyprus and Belize use the full figures, so ranking countries is not valid. Spain, France and Germany are mostly or wholly missing for the same reason. Venezuela is blank though its page prints USD (ConocoPhillips $30,305 million claimed, $8,366.1 million awarded). Cameroon ($1,112 million) and Congo ($1,584 million) are blank though their pages print amounts. One pending claim, Zeph v. Australia (I) at $198,202.4 million (confirmed on the page), is 27% of the whole layer and would set the colour scale. Fixable by rereading every country using UNCTAD's printed USD figure, or from the Excel file, with Australia handled as an outlier and pending claims stated.

totals.note: A case with several respondents counts once for each, and pages differ in age, so rows read and the UNCTAD total are not an exact match. UNCTAD's 136 countries plus the EU compares with 127 countries plus the EU here; Japan, Luxembourg and the United Kingdom account for 3 of the 9 missing.

unctad_top10_compare.label: UNCTAD IIA Issues Note 3, Nov 2024, Figure 4: most frequent respondents 1987-2023 (1,332 cases). The note lists labels and numbers separately; pairs were matched by order.
unctad_top10_compare.check: Figures reconfirmed in the note: all ten match the draft's unctad_2023 column, and read_now is equal or higher for each. No UNCTAD top ten for 2025 was found. Pages for Venezuela, Argentina, Mexico, Spain and Egypt were reopened and match read_now.

gaps: fdi_isds_cases is still partial: 1383 rows across 128 respondents including the EU, against UNCTAD 1,440 cases and 136 countries plus the EU at 31 July 2025, and 1,463 cases at 31 December 2025.

Search results list at least 9 case titles against Tanzania (not opened, not counted), so Tanzania is a real gap. Brazil, Guinea, Jamaica and others are unread, not zero. UNCTAD Policy Monitor 32 (Dec 2025) names Kosovo as a respondent; no Navigator page for it was found.

Cambodia was read from UNCTAD's test server because the main country address refused; its one case is confirmed on the main address case page (/cases/1186). Other pages on that server were refused by the permission check.

Rows passed through a summarising tool. Spot-check of 25 countries: all counts matched. Amounts are UNCTAD's figures as read; several cases show very large demands, such as Saba Fakes v. Turkey at 19,000 mln USD. Money layers are marked publish false.
Kept unchanged from round 24: other counts, flags and notes. Nine zeros removed; see unread.zeros_removed. Other country pages could miss cases the way Japan's did, though none did in the spot-check.
